newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus says missile system to cost $426 million.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus says missile system to cost $426 million.

text.p: Cyprus said on Wednesday a missile system it planned to buy from Russia would cost an estimated 200 million Cyprus pounds ($426 million).

The semi-official Cyprus News Agency quoted Yiannakis Cassoulides, Cypriot government spokesman, as saying the deal with Russia, which has angered Turkey, did not include a clause allowing the government to cancel the order.

He was asked by reporters what would happen if the S-300 anti-aircraft missiles were no longer needed when they arrived in 16 months' time because of a solution to the island's division between hostile Turkish Cypriot and Greek Cypriot communities.
Cassoulides replied that Cyprus would then have spent 200 million Cyprus pounds -- a price which he said was well worth paying to solve the island's 23-year division.
Ankara threatened several times last week to take military action if the S-300s were sent to Cyprus, where Turkey backs a Turkish Cypriot breakaway state in the north.

Cyprus has been divided since 1974 when Turkey invaded the north of the island after a coup in Nicosia engineered by the military junta then ruling Greece. Turkey has about 30,000 troops in the north while the internationally recognised Cypriot government has 11,500 in the south.
